transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-18
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lena Cho (Redwood SE), Jordan Mills (Redwood SE), Maria Gomez (Pioneer CISO), Daniel Reed (Pioneer CTO), Aisha Khan (Head of Cloud Ops), Tom Ellis (Procurement)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete):
- Pioneer Federal is evaluating Redwood for customer-facing and internal LLM features; primary concerns are EU data residency, HIPAA-adjacent controls for certain product lines, and strict logging restrictions for PCI/HIPAA regulated flows.
- Interested in Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) but open to Dedicated if isolation and key control are sufficient.
- Next steps: share security artifacts, schedule infra deep dive, provide compliance questionnaire answers.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir (Redwood): hey everybody, thanks for making time, this is Samir from Redwood, with Lena and Jordan, we're excited to learn about your requirements and walk through options for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
[00:12] Maria (Pioneer): thanks Samir, Maria here. quick context - we're a regional bank with branches across EU and US, we have a brand new chat assistant project and also some onboarding automation; compliance is number one for us so data residency and logging policies are critical.
[00:27] Daniel (Pioneer): yeah hi Daniel - CTO - we want to keep PII in EU for EU customers, and for some products we need HIPAA like safeguards, even though we're not a healthcare provider per se.
[00:39] Lena (Redwood): got it - thanks for the context. two quick clarifying questions: (1) are you currently using any hosted LLMs in production? (2) do you have an internal KMS or HSM for customer keys?
[00:50] Aisha (Pioneer): we run some prototypes on a public cloud provider, mostly OpenAI for prototyping; keys are in our cloud KMS (GCP KMS) and some keys are customer-specific. we have an HSM for payments and would prefer to reuse that if possible.
[01:05] Jordan (Redwood): ok, good detail. in Redwood, we support hosted (Redwood-managed), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools with tenant isolation), and Private (VPC or on-prem). for KMS you can either integrate your existing KMS/HSM for key wrapping, or we can use customer-managed keys in a private deployment.
[01:22] Maria (Pioneer): important: our compliance team will not allow raw transcript logs with PII to leave the EU. if you offer hosted, do you have an option to keep logs in-region and redact? Also what about audit logs and retention windows?
[01:36] Samir (Redwood): good question. hosted can be configured to store logs in region for enterprise customers, but out of the box hosted is global. for strict regulatory setups we usually recommend Dedicated with region pinning or Private deployment. we do offer configurable audit logging retention and redaction pipelines, and we can integrate redaction rules on the request side or via a post-process pipeline.
[01:55] Maria (interject): when you say redaction pipeline, is that automatic PII redaction? we need evidence for auditors.
[02:02] Lena (Redwood): yes, we have a pipeline that can do deterministic redaction based on patterns and also a heuristic PII detector; we can provide a runbook and examples. auditors usually ask for SOC2 controls + screenshots of pipeline configs. we'll share the SOC2 report and the redaction playbook.
[02:18] Tom (Pioneer): procurement question - cost wise, if we go Dedicated versus Private on-prem, what's the delta? we need some ballpark to model.
[02:25] Jordan (Redwood): rough rule: Dedicated (reserved) gives you predictable throughput and is cheaper than on-prem total cost of ownership usually — but Private/on-prem is higher CAPEX and operational overhead. Dedicated still has Redwood managing the runtime but with tenant isolation and options for customer-managed keys. We'll send a pricing sheet.
[02:42] Daniel (Pioneer): about network isolation - can Dedicated live inside our VPC or does it still route through Redwood public endpoints?
[02:50] Samir (Redwood): Dedicated typically runs in a Redwood-managed VPC per customer with private peering options; the Private offering gives you full control with a customer-managed control plane or on-prem package. For strict network controls we often recommend Private or our VPC peering model.
[03:08] Maria (Pioneer): GDPR question - do you support data subject access removal or deletion across logs/backups? we need to be sure we can delete EU subject data on request.
[03:18] Lena (Redwood): yes, we support data deletion APIs and can configure data lifecycle policies per region. backups are included in the lifecycle and can be isolated by region for EU. we'll share the lifecycle policy doc.
[03:30] Maria (Pioneer): also need to understand key management - if we bring our own KMS, how does key rotation and audit work? can you show how keys are used for encrypting token caches/KV cache?
[03:42] Jordan (Redwood): we never store plaintext keys. we use envelope encryption — customer-managed master key in your KMS wraps per-instance keys. KV cache (sorry KV cash in my notes) is encrypted at rest using those keys and ephemeral keys in memory. rotation is supported via key versioning and we can show rotation procedures.
[04:02] Aisha (Pioneer): there are strict logging restrictions for our payment flows: minimal logs, redaction, and certain events cannot be logged at all. is there a way to exclude endpoints or routes from logging?
[04:12] Lena (Redwood): yes you can configure per-route logging policies and disable token-level logs for specific routes. you can also route those requests to a Private deployment or a dedicated cluster with logging disabled.
[04:25] Maria (Pioneer): perfect. auditor will also ask for evidence of RBAC and SSO. do you integrate with our SAML provider and can you show role separation?
[04:34] Samir (Redwood): we integrate with SAML/SSO and support SAML-based provisioning, SCIM for group sync, and fine-grained RBAC. we can demo role-based consoles and audit trails.
[04:45] Tom (Pioneer): on legal, we need to know about data processor agreements and subprocessor lists. is that available?
[04:53] Samir (Redwood): yes, we have a DPA and a subprocessors list we can provide; we'll include that in the security pack.
[05:00] Daniel (Pioneer): what about SLA and failover? for customer facing stuff we need <200ms p95 latency and 99.9% uptime SLA, is that realistic?
[05:12] Jordan (Redwood): depends on model and prompt lengths. for low-latency use cases we recommend optimizing model choice and seq length, using batching controls, and Dedicated or Private with droplet placement. 200ms p95 for generation is aggressive for large models; for smaller models and shorter contexts it's achievable. we'll run benchmarks with your sample prompts.
[05:34] Maria (Pioneer): benchmarks — we will share a set of canonical prompts including PII-heavy samples and expected SLA metrics. will you be able to run them in an EU region?
[05:44] Lena (Redwood): yes, we can run benchmark runs in EU cluster for latency/throughput and provide a report. we'll also show cost per 1k tokens and per-call.
[05:55] Daniel (Pioneer): curious on fallback — if capacity constrained in EU, do you have automatic fallbacks that keep data in EU?
[06:05] Samir (Redwood): our smart routing can fallback to compatible model variants in the same region or to a dedicated reserved pool. if the only available capacity is outside EU, we can fail closed or route to a private pool depending on your policy.
[06:18] Maria (Pioneer): can you produce attestations for where data is processed and logs stored? auditors like a data map.
[06:26] Samir (Redwood): yes we can provide data flow diagrams and signed attestations as part of the enterprise package.
[06:32] Tom (Pioneer): procurement will need a timeline for pilot, legal review, and production roll-out — what's typical?
[06:40] Samir (Redwood): pilot can be as short as 2-4 weeks for a scoped POC (benchmarks + a small integration). legal and security review typically 2-6 weeks depending on complexity. dedicated or private provisioning also depends on capacity lead times.
[06:55] Aisha (Pioneer): a few technical Qs: do you support tenant-scoped metrics and per-customer billing exports?
[07:03] Jordan (Redwood): yes, per-tenant metrics, token-level billing exports, and CSV/BigQuery exports for cost analysis.
[07:12] Daniel (Pioneer): what about redaction accuracy? auditors will ask for false positive/negative rates on PII detection.
[07:20] Lena (Redwood): we can provide evaluation metrics from our PII detector and show sample runs. note that redaction is a best-effort; for high-risk flows we recommend pre-send client-side redaction or Private on-prem where you fully control the pipeline.
[07:38] Maria (Pioneer): HIPAA-ish question: do you have BAAs? we're not a covered entity but some of our partners require BAA-level controls.
[07:46] Samir (Redwood): Redwood can support BAA-like contractual terms for certain enterprise customers; we'll route that to legal and include in the security pack.
[07:55] Tom (Pioneer): is there a mechanism to prevent models from learning from customer data?
[08:02] Jordan (Redwood): yes, for enterprise deployments we provide a no-training promise for customer data and can disable telemetry/model improvement using your logs; we'll put that into contract language.
[08:12] Maria (Pioneer): fine-grained question on KMS integration for on-prem: can we retain full ownership of master keys and only allow Redwood to get wrapped keys?
[08:22] Lena (Redwood): absolutely, envelope encryption pattern allows the customer to keep master key in their HSM; Redwood only stores wrapped keys and ephemeral keys.
[08:30] Daniel (Pioneer): showstoppers: if our auditors demand zero external subprocessors for certain data flows, can you run a fully air-gapped on-prem instance?
[08:40] Samir (Redwood): yes we have an on-prem package for air-gapped deployments; it requires more lead time and support contract but it's doable.
[08:50] Aisha (Pioneer): about log retention policies — can you produce per-customer retention windows and automatic deletion?
[08:58] Jordan (Redwood): yes, retention policies are configurable per-customer and per-route; we can schedule automatic purges and provide deletion proofs.
[09:08] Maria (Pioneer): ok great. any weaknesses you want to call out upfront?
[09:14] Samir (Redwood): the main tradeoff is operational overhead vs control — Private/on-prem gives you ultimate control but requires more ops. Dedicated is often a good middle ground. for extreme low-latency and very large models public hosted may not meet strict p95 targets.
[09:30] Tom (Pioneer): procurement note: we'll want redacted sample logs and a dry run of the DPA.
[09:36] Samir (Redwood): understood, we'll include sample redacted logs and a draft DPA.
[09:42] Daniel (Pioneer): do you do penetration testing or accept customer pentest reports?
[09:48] Lena (Redwood): we do third-party pentests and can share summaries; for enterprise customers we have an option to allow limited scoped customer-led tests.
[09:58] Maria (Pioneer): fine. can you confirm support for EU data residency at rest and in transit?
[10:04] Jordan (Redwood): yes we support in-transit encryption (TLS) and encryption at rest per-region; EU clusters store data at rest in EU as configured.
[10:14] Samir (Redwood): to be explicit: options are (1) Hosted with region pinning for logs and data (enterprise tier), (2) Dedicated reserved pools with VPC peering and customer-managed KMS, (3) Private VPC/on-prem for maximum control. we'll include a decision matrix.
[10:35] Aisha (Pioneer): what's the onboarding time for a Dedicated EU cluster?
[10:40] Jordan (Redwood): typically 2-4 weeks depending on GPU availability and network peering.
[10:46] Maria (Pioneer): we will need evidence artifacts: SOC2, ISO, pen test, subprocessors list, DPA.
[10:55] Samir (Redwood): we'll package those and send today/tomorrow.
[11:00] Tom (Pioneer): last q - do you have sample contract language for no-training and data deletion?
[11:06] Samir (Redwood): yes we'll include contract snippets.
[11:10] Daniel (Pioneer): ok we'll circulate internal stakeholders and get back with the compliance questionnaire.
[11:16] Samir (Redwood): great, thank you everyone. recap and next steps coming from us.
